questions.stem: What is the result of the expression `true && false || true`?
questions.solution: The logical AND operator (`&&`) has higher precedence than the logical OR operator (`||`). First, `true && false` evaluates to `false`, then `false || true` evaluates to `true`. So the result is `true`.
questions.explanation: Precedence rules determine the order of evaluation in an expression. In this case, the AND operation is performed before the OR operation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to evaluate left-to-right without considering operator precedence, which would lead to selecting 'A: false'.

questions.stem: What is the result of the expression `false || true && false`?
questions.solution: The logical OR operator (`||`) has lower precedence than the logical AND operator (`&&`). First, `true && false` evaluates to `false`, then `false || false` evaluates to `false`. So the result is `false`.
questions.explanation: Operator precedence governs the sequence of operations. In this case, the OR operation happens after the AND operation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to evaluate right-to-left without considering operator precedence, which would lead to selecting 'A: true'.

questions.stem: What is the result of the expression `(true && false) || true`?
questions.solution: The parentheses group the `true && false` part, so it's evaluated first as `false`. Then `false || true` evaluates to `true`. So the result is `true`.
questions.explanation: Parentheses can be used to override operator precedence and force specific parts of an expression to be evaluated first.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to assume that the parentheses don't change the order of evaluation, which would lead to selecting 'A: false'.

questions.stem: What is the result of the expression `!true && !false`?
questions.solution: The logical NOT operator (`!`) has higher precedence than the logical AND operator (`&&`). First, `!true` evaluates to `false`, then `false && !false` evaluates to `false`. So the result is `false`.
questions.explanation: Operator precedence applies to both prefix and infix operators. In this case, the NOT operation happens before the AND operation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to evaluate left-to-right without considering operator precedence, which would lead to selecting 'A: true'.

questions.stem: What is the result of the expression `!false || !true`?
questions.solution: The logical NOT operator (`!`) has higher precedence than the logical OR operator (`||`). First, `!false` evaluates to `true`, then `true || !true` evaluates to `true`. So the result is `true`.
questions.explanation: Operator precedence applies to both prefix and infix operators. In this case, the NOT operation happens before the OR operation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to evaluate right-to-left without considering operator precedence, which would lead to selecting 'B: false'.

questions.stem: What is the result of the expression `!true && (false || true)`?
questions.solution: The logical NOT operator (`!`) has higher precedence than the logical AND operator (`&&`). First, `!true` evaluates to `false`. The parentheses group the `false || true` part, which evaluates to `true`. Then `false && true` evaluates to `false`. So the result is `false`.
questions.explanation: Operator precedence and parentheses can be combined in expressions. In this case, the NOT operation happens first, followed by the OR within parentheses, and finally the AND operation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to evaluate without considering operator precedence or the effect of parentheses, which could lead to selecting 'A: true'.

questions.stem: What is the result of the expression `(true && !false) || (false && !true)`?
questions.solution: The parentheses group the expressions, and within each group, the NOT operator has higher precedence than the AND operator. The first group evaluates to `true`, and the second group evaluates to `false`. Then `true || false` evaluates to `true`. So the result is `true`.
questions.explanation: Operator precedence and parentheses can be combined in expressions. In this case, each set of parentheses contains a NOT operation followed by an AND operation, with the OR operation happening last.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to evaluate without considering operator precedence or the effect of parentheses, which could lead to selecting 'B: false'.
